candidate_sources.title: Alternaria Leaf Spot of Brassicas | Cornell Vegetables
candidate_sources.snippet: Alternaria leaf spot is a common foliar disease of brassica crops caused by the fungal pathogen Alternaria brassicicola. The first symptoms to appear are pin-sized black specks found on the leaf surface or stem, which enlarge concentrically, creating a distinct target spot or bull's eye lesion with a yellow halo. Symptoms are typically seen on older, lower leaves first and can appear on cauliflower curds or broccoli heads in addition to the leaves.

candidate_sources.title: Alternaria leaf spot and head rot of Brassica crops | UMN Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Alternaria leaf spot and head rot of Brassica crops including cauliflower. Caused by Alternaria brassicicola and Alternaria brassicae. Spores are produced after exposure to high relative humidity (~87%) and temperatures between 68-86 °F. Discusses identification, biology, and management strategies including seed treatment, crop rotation, and fungicide applications.

candidate_sources.title: Cabbage and Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea)-Alternaria Diseases (Black Spot, Gray Leaf Spot, Pod Spot) | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Alternaria diseases of cabbage and cauliflower including black spot, gray leaf spot, and pod spot. Caused by Alternaria brassicae and Alternaria brassicicola. Symptoms include small dark spots that enlarge into target-like lesions with concentric rings on leaves, stems, and curds. Includes cultural and chemical control recommendations for the Pacific Northwest.

candidate_sources.title: Cabbage and Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea)-Bacterial Soft Rot Erwinia | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbook entry dedicated to Bacterial Soft Rot (Erwinia) on cabbage and cauliflower, with symptoms, causal agent, and management recommendations.

candidate_sources.title: Bacterial Soft Rot – Wisconsin Horticulture
candidate_sources.snippet: Soft rots initially cause water-soaked spots that enlarge, become sunken and soft, with interior tissues becoming mushy and discolored. Caused by Pectobacterium carotovorum (previously Erwinia carotovora), Dickeya species, and certain Pseudomonas, Bacillus and Clostridium species. Bacteria enter through wounds and natural openings.

candidate_sources.title: Bacterial Soft Rot | USU Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Utah State University Extension factsheet on bacterial soft rot of vegetables including crucifers such as cauliflower. Covers symptoms (water-soaked, mushy tissue with foul odor), pathogens (Pectobacterium/Erwinia), conditions favoring disease, and cultural management.

candidate_sources.title: Bacterial leaf spot on cauliflower | Long Island Vegetable Health
candidate_sources.snippet: Bacterial leaf spot on cauliflower - Cornell Long Island Vegetable Pathology entry covering symptoms (angular, water-soaked lesions), pathogen identity and diagnostic images specific to cauliflower.

candidate_sources.title: First Report of Bacterial Blight of Romanesco Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis) Caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. alisalensis in California | Plant Disease
candidate_sources.snippet: APS Plant Disease peer-reviewed report of bacterial blight/leaf spot on cauliflower caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. alisalensis — small angular water-soaked flecks developing into tan-to-gray angular lesions up to 5 mm with chlorotic borders.

candidate_sources.title: Pectobacterium carotovorum (bacterial soft rot) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet for Pectobacterium carotovorum, the causal agent of bacterial soft rot on cauliflower and other brassicas — pathogen description, host range, symptoms, epidemiology, and management.

candidate_sources.title: Black Rot of Brassicas | NC State Extension Publications
candidate_sources.snippet: NC State Extension factsheet describing black rot of brassicas caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris, covering symptoms (V-shaped yellow lesions, blackened veins), pathogen biology, and management practices on cabbage, cauliflower, and other crucifers.

candidate_sources.title: Cabbage and Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea)-Black Rot | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: PNW Pest Management Handbook entry dedicated to Black Rot on cabbage and cauliflower, describing the causal agent Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris, V-shaped chlorotic lesions with blackened veins, seed-borne transmission, and integrated management including hot-water seed treatment and Actigard applications.

candidate_sources.title: Practical and Comprehensive Diagnostic Guide for Black Rot of Brassicas | Plant Health Progress
candidate_sources.snippet: APS Plant Health Progress diagnostic guide for black rot of brassicas including cauliflower, providing comprehensive coverage of Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris symptomatology, diagnostics, epidemiology, and management recommendations.

candidate_sources.title: Brassicas, Black Rot | UMass Center for Agriculture, Food, and the Environment
candidate_sources.snippet: UMass Extension vegetable factsheet dedicated to Black Rot of brassicas (including cauliflower), detailing symptoms such as V-shaped yellow lesions with blackened veins, pathogen Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris, disease cycle, and management through clean seed, crop rotation, and hot-water seed treatment.

candidate_sources.title: Downy Mildew on Brassica Crops | NC State Extension Publications
candidate_sources.snippet: Symptoms on older leaves appear as small, angular, light green to yellow lesions on the upper leaf surface; white fluffy growth of the pathogen develops on the undersides of leaves. The curds of cauliflower can be infected in the field and in storage. Caused by Peronospora parasitica (= Hyaloperonospora parasitica). Management includes rotation to non-cruciferous crops for 2-3 years and sanitation practices.

candidate_sources.title: Brassicas, Downy Mildew : Vegetable : Center for Agriculture, Food, and the Environment (CAFE) at UMass Amherst
candidate_sources.snippet: Downy mildew on brassica crops is caused by the oomycete Hyaloperonospora parasitica. Management programs should include a rotation away from brassica crops for at least three years. Plant cauliflower in well-drained fields with good air circulation to reduce the likelihood of infection.

candidate_sources.title: Cabbage and Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea)-Downy Mildew (Staghead) | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbook entry dedicated to Downy Mildew (Staghead) on Cabbage and Cauliflower caused by Hyaloperonospora parasitica. Includes symptoms, disease cycle, cultural and chemical control recommendations for brassica crops in the Pacific Northwest.

candidate_sources.title: Downy Mildew / Cole Crops / Agriculture: Pest Management Guidelines / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines for Downy Mildew on cole crops including cauliflower. Abundant sporulation and rapid disease development occur at greater than 98% relative humidity and temperatures between 46-60°F. Includes integrated management recommendations.
